content:
Several people have been trying to streamline the algebra hierarchy recently. The back story for my personal motivation is that instance inference for adeles is slow and we have a bunch of material in FLT which I'm too embarrassed to PR until I've understood properly why it's slow.

I want to ask specifically here about fast_instance%. Currently I run into instance traces where I see lets and think "hmm, that's probably a missing fast_instance%, maybe we should remove them". Here are some I ran into yesterday (the first three of which are #39773):

docs#Pi.monoid has no fast_instance%. If we add it then it changes from

@[implicit_reducible, expose] def Pi.monoid.{u, v₁} : {I : Type u} →
  {f : I → Type v₁} → [(i : I) → Monoid (f i)] → Monoid ((i : I) → f i) :=
fun {I} {f} [(i : I) → Monoid (f i)] ↦
  let __spread.0 := semigroup;
  let __spread.1 := mulOneClass;
  { toSemigroup := __spread.0, toOne := __spread.1.toOne, one_mul := ⋯, mul_one := ⋯, npow := fun n x i ↦ x i ^ n,
    npow_zero := ⋯, npow_succ := ⋯ }

to

@[implicit_reducible, expose] def Pi.monoid.{u, v₁} : {I : Type u} →
  {f : I → Type v₁} → [(i : I) → Monoid (f i)] → Monoid ((i : I) → f i) :=
fun {I} {f} [(i : I) → Monoid (f i)] ↦
  { toSemigroup := semigroup, toOne := instOne, one_mul := ⋯, mul_one := ⋯, npow := fun a a_1 i ↦ Monoid.npow a (a_1 i),
    npow_zero := ⋯, npow_succ := ⋯ }

That looks better to me but is it marginal?

Next in the same file is docs#Pi.commMonoid . If we add fast_instance% it goes from

@[implicit_reducible, expose] def Pi.commMonoid.{u, v₁} : {I : Type u} →
  {f : I → Type v₁} → [(i : I) → CommMonoid (f i)] → CommMonoid ((i : I) → f i) :=
fun {I} {f} [(i : I) → CommMonoid (f i)] ↦
  let __src := monoid;
  have __src_1 := commSemigroup;
  { toMonoid := __src, mul_comm := ⋯ }

to

@[implicit_reducible, expose] def Pi.commMonoid.{u, v₁} : {I : Type u} →
  {f : I → Type v₁} → [(i : I) → CommMonoid (f i)] → CommMonoid ((i : I) → f i) :=
fun {I} {f} [(i : I) → CommMonoid (f i)] ↦ { toMonoid := monoid, mul_comm := ⋯ }

This one looks marginal as well but again it's removing a spurious let and my feeling is that this is at worst neutral and perhaps sometimes better (perhaps a let will occasionally stop two things being syntactically equal, for example?).

Another one I ran into yesterday is docs#Multiplicative.monoid . A fast_instance% takes it from

@[implicit_reducible, expose] def Multiplicative.monoid.{u} : {α : Type u} →
  [h : AddMonoid α] → Monoid (Multiplicative α) :=
fun {α} [AddMonoid α] ↦
  let __src := Multiplicative.mulOneClass;
  have __src_1 := Multiplicative.semigroup;
  { toMul := __src.toMul, mul_assoc := ⋯, toOne := __src.toOne, one_mul := ⋯, mul_one := ⋯, npow := AddMonoid.nsmul,
    npow_zero := ⋯, npow_succ := ⋯ }

to

@[implicit_reducible, expose] def Multiplicative.monoid.{u} : {α : Type u} →
  [h : AddMonoid α] → Monoid (Multiplicative α) :=
fun {α} [AddMonoid α] ↦
  { toSemigroup := Multiplicative.semigroup, toOne := instOneMultiplicativeOfZero, one_mul := ⋯, mul_one := ⋯,
    npow := fun a a_1 ↦ AddMonoid.nsmul a a_1, npow_zero := ⋯, npow_succ := ⋯ }

Again this looks better.

Another one perhaps worth looking at is docs#Module.compHom which goes from

@[reducible, expose] def Module.compHom.{u_1, u_2, u_3} : {R : Type u_1} →
  {S : Type u_2} →
    (M : Type u_3) →
      [inst : Semiring R] →
        [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] → [Module R M] → [inst_3 : Semiring S] → (S →+* R) → Module S M :=
fun {R} {S} M [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Semiring S] f ↦
  let __src := MulActionWithZero.compHom M f.toMonoidWithZeroHom;
  have __src_1 := DistribMulAction.compHom M ↑f;
  { toMulAction := __src.toMulAction, smul_zero := ⋯, smul_add := ⋯, add_smul := ⋯, zero_smul := ⋯ }

to

@[reducible, expose] def Module.compHom.{u_1, u_2, u_3} : {R : Type u_1} →
  {S : Type u_2} →
    (M : Type u_3) →
      [inst : Semiring R] →
        [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] → [Module R M] → [inst_3 : Semiring S] → (S →+* R) → Module S M :=
fun {R} {S} M [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Semiring S] f ↦
  { smul := fun a a_1 ↦ SMul.smul (↑f.toMonoidWithZeroHom a) a_1, mul_smul := ⋯, one_smul := ⋯, smul_zero := ⋯,
    smul_add := ⋯, add_smul := ⋯, zero_smul := ⋯ }

which again has fewer lets but to be honest I'm just confused about that one.

Let me talk about some even more marginal changes which one could make. docs#Pi.instMul is [∀ i, Mul (M i)] : Mul (∀ i, M i) and fast_instance% even changes this, from

fun {ι} {M} [(i : ι) → Mul (M i)] ↦ { mul := fun a a_1 i ↦ Mul.mul (a i) (a_1 i) }

to

fun {ι} {M} [(i : ι) → Mul (M i)] ↦ { mul := fun f g i ↦ f i * g i }

That really is a change -- it's gone from Mul.mul to HMul.hMul. Similarly adding fast_instance% to Pi.instOne changes the 1 from
fun i ↦ @OfNat.ofNat (M i) 1 One.toOfNat1 to fun i ↦ One.one.

My questions:
(1) Is it worth changing these sorts of instances as I run into them or is there an argument against making our codebase look a bit more complicated with all this weird fast_instance% stuff? Note that the benchmark in #39773 which changes the first three (Pi.monoid, Pi.commMonoid, Multiplicative.monoid) is -32G, which is negligible, but probably not noise.
(2) Is it worth sweeping mathlib for fast_instance% somehow? Should _every_ instance be a fast_instance% in some sense? Could one write code to make this happen and try it?

I think there is no clear answer to these questions. It might be an interesting experiment to try (2). E.g. we could define a fast_instance command in place of the instance command, and then put this everywhere in mathlib.
I am testing this in #39780 (my script has not finished yet, so this is just to give an idea).
I will be offline for a couple of hours, so I am letting it run, but the PR gives an idea of the modifications

Right now things are building, but there are >= 5 files where the long line linter is complaining and the "Lint style" test is failing because there's an undocumented script in scripts/ . Do you think that either of these will stop !radar from working?
I've pushed all the changes. Making it green now and benching again
I thought I benched it? Currently trying to work out why Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Valued/WithVal.lean got faster and trying to isolate the changes which caused it.
I add more fast_instance after you bench it. There were some errors but it now compiles locally. Benching again.
It's benched. Results are mixed, some files got better and other got slower. I am opening another PR keeping only the green files, we can then maybe use slice bot on that one to open small PRs.
I already opened the one which made WithVal 12% faster (because I use this file in FLT)
Merging that one, it seems a clear win.

#39814 is much better. If someone wants to investigate what's happening to Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Group.Seminorm it would be nice (the file is not touched by the PR, but Mathlib/Analysis/Seminorm is).

+659.5M (the change in Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Group.Seminorm) is surely just noise. Take any random PR which has been !radar'ed, and sort by changes. You will see 170 pages of changes, which start with changes of this magnitude.
@Riccardo Brasca I made one for you. #39827 adds a comment to a module docstring in a leaf file. Here are the first and last of the 170 pages of changes in radar:
I anyway tried in #39846 to revert the changes to Mathlib.Analysis.Seminormand radar says -192.8G, while for #39814 it says -79.8G. This is surely not noise, so something is happening here.
I've opened #39929 that is the most convincing win.
